guide.prompt: Use case: style-transfer identity preprocessing for a reusable pet template pipeline. Image 1 is the sole authority for visual medium and stylization only: copy its brushwork, line language, pigment behavior, edge treatment, texture scale, shape simplification, facial abstraction, anatomical stylization, local contrast and degree of realism. Image 2 is the sole authority for pet identity only: preserve its adult breed, coat pattern, markings, ear shape, eye color, muzzle proportions and healthy mature body type. Create one clean centered subject study of the pet from Image 2, fully redrawn through Image 1's non-photographic visual language. Use a plain unobtrusive background and do not copy Image 1's scene, pose, costume, props, text or layout. The pet must look drawn, painted or sculpted by the same visual system as Image 1 before it enters the final scene. Replace literal fur strands with the reference's marks and shapes; replace photographic eyes, wet nose highlights, lens lighting and realistic facial volume with the reference's stylized equivalents. Keep the pet recognizable, appealing, adult and healthy. No puppy or kitten proportions, no photorealistic face, no studio-photo lighting, no shallow depth of field, no realistic fur microtexture, no text, no logo and no watermark. Identity: adult adult seal-point Ragdoll cat; cream long coat, deep seal-brown mask and ears, round blue eyes, broad fluffy cheeks, dark nose, full chest and healthy adult body. Return only the finished pre-stylized identity guide.

Replace literal fur strands with large soft marks and flowing painted shapes, stylized whiskers, stylized eyes and nose, no studio lighting, no lens effects, no depth-of-field blur, no realistic fur microtexture. Keep one unobtrusive plain background and a centered single-animal composition suitable as a reusable identity guide. Do not include props, text, logos, watermarks, or any scene from the reference. The cat should look elegant, recognizable, adult, healthy, and clearly drawn/painted rather than photographic.
